dial.summary: Accumulation conditions intact as of August 25: BTC at ~$78,944, BTC.D at 58.8% (firm above 55%), funding rates near zero; Consumer Confidence released below consensus today; PCE and GDP 2nd estimate tomorrow (August 26) are the critical next macro gate ahead of Jackson Hole (August 27–29) and Warsh's inaugural keynote (August 28); 2s10s spread at +47bps with 4-week steepening trend intact; DXY at 98.96 (neutral band, 4-week down); real yields unchanged at 2.35% (headwind above 2%); global liquidity expanding — the PCE/Jackson Hole/NFP trifecta and FOMC September 15–16 are the structural decision points ahead.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$102.7T as of June 2026 (latest available — ~6-week reporting lag); US M2 at $23,155.20B ($23.155T) for June 2026, +5.5% YoY (record high, 28th consecutive monthly increase); no YoY contraction signal from any major central bank; 4-week trend up based on sustained US M2 expansion and continued global central bank balance sheet stability; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY contraction headwind condition not triggered).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading — August 2026 data releases September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8% (first factory hiring expansion in 18 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; July reading is the highest since May 2022; 4-week trend up: June 53.3% → July 55.6% = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 98.96 on August 25, 2026 (up slightly from 98.84 on August 24); 4-week trend down: DXY weakened approximately 2.5% over the past month (from ~101.4–101.5 around July 25 to 98.96 on August 25), well above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by US Treasury's expanded long-term buyback program and rate cut expectations; status NEUTRAL (ICE DXY in the 97.5–100 neutral band; a sustained close below 97.5 would flip to supportive; PCE August 26 and Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28 are key directional catalysts).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.35% as of August 22, 2026 (latest available); 4-week trend down: 10-year TIPS auction cleared at 2.44% on July 23, 2026 → DFII10 at 2.35% on August 22 = -9bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold despite falling trend; soft PCE on August 26 and dovish Warsh keynote August 28 are the catalysts needed to compress real yields meaningfully below 2%).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 25, 2026: 10Y yield at 4.71%, 2Y yield at 4.24%; spread = +47bps (narrowed from +51bps on August 24 as the 10Y leg fell 3bps and 2Y rose 1bp); 4-week trend up: ~+35bps (July 24) → +47bps (August 25) = +12bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND sustained 4-week steepening trend intact; PCE August 26 and Warsh tone August 28 are the next key curve inputs).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,745,699M (~$6.75T) for week ending August 19, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 20); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (August 5) → $6.75T (August 19) = +$50B (+0.7%), near the 0.5% flat threshold; balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal; status supportive.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate near zero at approximately +0.0025% to +0.0069%/8h across major exchanges (Binance, Bybit, OKX) as of August 21–25, 2026; BTC price ~$78,944 (August 24–25), up from ~$77,300 prior week; funding remained flat-to-near-zero despite price appreciation — a textbook accumulation signature (price up, funding flat); well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; 30-day trend down vs late-June/early-July elevated levels; status supportive.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$304B (CoinGecko, August 25, 2026); total crypto market cap ~$2.68T; stablecoin dominance 11.35% per CoinGecko Aug 25 data (down from 11.45% on August 24); BTC.D at 58.8% (firm above 55%); 30-day trend down: ~13–14% (July 25) → 11.35% (August 25) — capital rotating from stablecoins into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL rises — is opposite of current dynamics).

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays at 8:30 AM ET — July PCE Price Index (Fed's preferred inflation gauge), Personal Income, and Personal Spending; arrives one day before Jackson Hole opens; hot core CPI (3.1% YoY, August 12) implies core PCE potentially 2.7–2.8% YoY; a reading above 2.8% strongly supports a September hike; a soft print (<2.5%) preserves the rate-cut path and could push DXY below 97.5 from current 98.96 — the single most important data print ahead of Jackson Hole.

upcoming.title: GDP 2nd Estimate (Q2 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA releases the second estimate of Q2 2026 GDP at 8:30 AM ET alongside July PCE, one day before Jackson Hole opens; July NFP shock (−23K) and hot core CPI (3.1%) have raised Q3 recession concerns; significant downward revisions alongside soft labor and hot inflation would reinforce the stagflation narrative and set the tone for Warsh's keynote the following morning.

upcoming.title: Jackson Hole Economic Symposium Opens (August 27–29)
upcoming.note: Kansas City Fed annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium begins at Jackson Lake Lodge, Wyoming — runs August 27–29; by the time proceedings open, markets will have processed PCE (August 26), GDP Q2 2nd estimate (August 26), Consumer Confidence (August 25), and Flash PMI (August 21); Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole keynote Friday morning August 28; FOMC September 15–16 is the next binding commitment.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 22, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 22, 2026 — released the opening morning of Jackson Hole; a sustained rise in claims arriving as Jackson Hole opens would immediately shape the tone for Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural keynote the next morning (August 28); context: July NFP shocked at −23K, making weekly claims particularly closely watched.

upcoming.title: Fed Chair Warsh Inaugural Jackson Hole Keynote
upcoming.note: Kevin Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole address Friday morning August 28 — the single most important macro event of this cycle for the crypto risk framework; all macro inputs will be in hand by then (PCE Aug 26, GDP 2nd estimate Aug 26, Consumer Confidence Aug 25); real yields at 2.35% showing a 4-week downtrend and DXY sliding (from ~101.5 to 98.96 over 30 days); a hawkish tone would sharply pressure risk assets; a neutral or dovish tone alongside soft PCE would be the macro green light to extend BTC's rally toward new all-time highs; September 15–16 FOMC is the next binding commitment.

upcoming.title: Chicago PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Chicago Business Barometer for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — released on the last business day of August (Monday August 31); regional manufacturing cross-check against July ISM surge (55.6%) and Flash PMI (August 21); a reading above 50 would reinforce broad manufacturing expansion heading into the September 1 ISM release and pre-FOMC September 15–16 positioning.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Manufacturing PMI Report on Business at 10:00 AM ET — first post-Jackson Hole activity read; July 2026 ISM came in at 55.6% (highest since May 2022); the August read arrives after the decisive PCE/GDP/Jackson Hole cluster (August 26–28) and will shape pre-FOMC September 15–16 positioning; a sustained expansion above 50 reinforces risk asset positioning; a collapse below 50 alongside a hawkish Warsh tone would pressure a Risk Off reassessment.
